measures.title: Imperial County Public Safety Sales and Use Tax Initiative
measures.summary: Asks whether to add a half-cent sales and use tax throughout Imperial County, including the cities, for 20 years, generating about $20 million a year. Per County Counsel's impartial analysis, the money goes into a Public Safety Fund limited to building and maintaining public safety facilities such as fire stations, law enforcement facilities and a coroner's facility, buying fire safety vehicles and equipment, and related costs, with a 7-member citizens' oversight committee and annual audits. It was placed on the ballot by voter petition.
measures.yesMeans: A half-cent sales tax for public safety is added countywide for 20 years.
measures.noMeans: The half-cent sales tax is not added.

measures.title: El Centro Public Safety/City Services Measure
measures.summary: Asks whether El Centro should add a new half-cent (0.5%) sales tax on top of its existing 0.5% city sales tax, for a total city rate of 1%, until ended by voters. Per the City Attorney's impartial analysis, it is a general tax raising about $8.4 million a year that goes into the city's general fund for any city purpose, with annual independent audits; the ballot question lists 911 response, police, fire and paramedics, streets, parks, homelessness and youth, senior and library programs.
measures.yesMeans: El Centro adds a half-cent sales tax with no end date.
measures.noMeans: The added half-cent sales tax is not approved.
